title: Single unreplicated working copy; recovery locations named in reports do not exist
observed_fact: ~/Projects/Train_automation and ~/iCloud Drive (Archive)/Desktop/Train_automation are absent. The iCloud shadow copy holds 1 file under data/raw/layer_b and no docs or ground truth. 108 untracked paths (all fusion, simulation, experiments, evaluation, annotation code; 18 of 20 scripts; all candidate annotations) exist only in ~/Desktop/Train_automation. origin/main holds 223 files at d4db94d.
why_it_matters: One disk fault, sync event or mistaken cleanup destroys the research code, 3.6 GB of original video and every candidate annotation. The directory already vanished once.

title: 73 index entries flagged assume-unchanged; 68 tracked files missing from disk and hidden from git status
evidence: git ls-files -v (73 'h'); git ls-files -d (68); git status shows only 10 M / 108 ??
observed_fact: Missing tracked files include configs/{audio,fusion,simulation,vision}.yaml, pyproject.toml, 10 package __init__.py files, src/railway_detection/__main__.py, vision/adapter.py, audio/noise_mixer.py, 12 test modules and tests/fixtures/mock_data.py. Five flagged files exist and were rewritten on 2026-10-13 (config/__init__.py, config/exceptions.py, data/sync.py, fusion/__init__.py, fusion/evidence.py) so their divergence from HEAD is also hidden.

dependencies_affected_outputs: IMA-03, IMA-43; every claim that the tree matches d4db94d
recommended_correction: Clear the assume-unchanged flags, diff the 5 present files against HEAD, restore only the 68 absent files from HEAD, never overwrite an existing file.

title: No working, reproducible Python environment; the environment that produced today's outputs is unrecorded
evidence: .venv/pyvenv.cfg; .venv/bin (no pip/pytest launchers); import torch fails with ModuleNotFoundError torch.torch_version; interpreter survey

There is no lock file and pyproject.toml is absent from disk. dist-info shows torch 2.13.0, ultralytics 8.4.121, numpy 2.4.6, opencv-python 5.0.0.93 under Python 3.11.

recommended_correction: Build a fresh venv outside any synced folder from restored pyproject.toml, pin with a lock file, record versions in every run manifest.
closure_test_or_evidence: Import check passes; pytest --collect-only reports zero import errors; lock file committed.

title: Recovery reports contain statements contradicted by the filesystem
observed_fact: Stated target path does not exist; docs/archive/git_baseline_d4db94d/ (claimed backup of 9 baseline files) does not exist; 'Zero auto-approvals were made' conflicts with 27 review files marked APPROVED (IMA-06); 'Zero project assets are missing' conflicts with IMA-02 and IMA-05; 9 modified tracked files reported, 10 present.
why_it_matters: These reports are the record of the incident. They cannot be used as evidence of integrity.
recommended_correction: Do not edit them. Qualify them in the supersession table of the master audit; replace with a hash manifest generated in Phase 0.
closure_test_or_evidence: EVIDENCE_MANIFEST exists and is the cited integrity record.

title: Vision training labels and data.yaml absent from disk
evidence: find data/raw/vision -name '*.txt' (0 files); no *.yaml under data/raw/vision; results/dataset_validation/dataset_manifest.jsonl (tracked)
observed_fact: 3,157 images are present but no YOLO label files and no dataset yaml. Boxes survive only inside the tracked manifest. negative_sample_count is 0.
why_it_matters: The vision model cannot be retrained or re-evaluated as-is; class-name provenance rests on the manifest (front=0, rear=1, side=2) and on labels observed in cached outputs.
recommended_correction: No action needed for the primary study. Record the limitation; regenerate labels from the manifest only if retraining becomes necessary.
closure_test_or_evidence: Limitation stated in the paper's data section.

title: All 27 review records are marked APPROVED by 'human_researcher_lead' although no human approval has occurred
evidence: data/ground_truth/reviews/*/event_*_review.json (adjudication_status, reviewer_metadata); tally: 27 APPROVED, 154 accepted + 46 marked_unobservable, 0 corrected
observed_fact: Every review file carries adjudication_status APPROVED, reviewer_id human_researcher_lead, inspection_tool 'ffmpeg-frame-analyzer / scipy-spectral-auditor v2.0', dated 2026-10-12T16:xx, and references a superseded proposal (v1 or v5) generated before the current v2-v6 candidates (17:10).
why_it_matters: A loader that trusts an 'APPROVED' field would ingest machine-written labels as certified ground truth. The approval firewall is currently a naming convention, not a control.
recommended_correction: Leave files untouched. Add an additive invalidation record listing their hashes. The ground-truth loader must accept only files listed in a new researcher-signed approval manifest and must reject any file on the invalidation list.
closure_test_or_evidence: Loader test: pointing the loader at data/ground_truth/reviews raises; only manifest-listed files load.

title: Current candidate timestamps and metadata show template-like regularity
observed_fact: T2 minus T1 is 0.7, 0.8 or 0.9 s in 22 of 22 events (0.8 s in 18). Events 009, 015 and 016 share the identical triple T0=1.5, T1=4.2, T2=5.0. Every proposal, including the seven recorded on 2026-10-04 after 19:20 local, carries recording_session_id 'session_20260914_morning'.
why_it_matters: Train speed and geometry vary, so a near-constant entry-to-occupancy interval is unlikely to be measured. If labels are formulaic, every ground-truth metric is meaningless.
recommended_correction: Human frame-by-frame review of every boundary with frame evidence captured per marker. Do not regenerate candidates automatically.
closure_test_or_evidence: Approved file per event carries frame index, reviewer, and a saved evidence frame per marker; distribution of T2-T1 reported in the annotation audit.

title: Censored boundaries are encoded as observed numeric values
evidence: data/ground_truth/proposals/engine_events/event_001_proposal_v3.json (T1, T2 = 0.0, candidate_observable true, rationale 'Left-censored'); T0 = 0.0 in 20 of 23 train proposals
observed_fact: Left-censoring is expressed only in free-text rationale while value_s is 0.0 and candidate_observable is true.
why_it_matters: Any evaluator reading value_s would treat a censored bound as an exact time and score a miss at t=0.
recommended_correction: Approved schema carries an explicit censoring field (none, left, right) per marker; value is a bound when censored; evaluator branches on the field.
closure_test_or_evidence: Schema validation rejects a marker whose rationale or flag indicates censoring without the censoring field set; evaluator unit tests cover each censoring case.

title: Engine-only candidate cites a detector confidence and has an unresolved T3/T4 definition
observed_fact: The v3 rationale refers to a detection confidence, which suggests model output was visible to the annotation assistant. T3 is placed on the front camera at 6.2 s, T4 is marked unobservable on the back camera, while the review record asserts T4 = 6.2.
why_it_matters: Annotation must be independent of the evaluated models. The engine-only event needs one unambiguous rule.
recommended_correction: Researcher re-annotates the engine event from raw frames only and fixes the rule (see EXPERIMENT_DESIGN_FINAL section 7.4).
closure_test_or_evidence: Approved engine-event file with no reference to model output.

title: Horn labels are spectral candidates, not audibly verified
evidence: proposals/*/..._proposal_v*.json confidence_note ('Researcher must perform listening check'); reviews/PHASE2_VERIFICATION_REPORT.md:191,214
observed_fact: 13 train events carry horn_status 'present' from spectral peaks. The project's own report notes road vehicles produce similar 300-800 Hz peaks.
why_it_matters: Horn recall, horn onset and any audio lead-time claim need audible confirmation.
recommended_correction: Researcher listening pass; three-valued label (present, absent, uncertain) with onset only when present.
closure_test_or_evidence: Approved horn field per event with listener initials.

title: Cross-camera fusion uses a hardcoded zero offset that the media metadata contradicts
observed_fact: The collector is built without a SyncAligner, so camera_1 and camera_2 records are merged as if both files began at the same instant. Recording start tags differ by 0 to 33 s per event (for example event_001 front 14:13:33, back 14:13:41; event_015 12 s; event_010 minus 17 s; event_008 33 s). Candidate T1/T2 are on the front clock and T3/T4 on the back clock, and experiments/runner.py:88-95 would place both on the fused timeline.
why_it_matters: Every dual-camera fused decision trace, and every interval that spans front and back markers (occupancy, premature opening, excess closure, clearance latency), is computed on an invalid timeline.
recommended_correction: Estimate per-event offsets empirically by audio cross-correlation with stated uncertainty and human acceptance; fuse only accepted events; otherwise run the independent-camera design.
closure_test_or_evidence: data/sync/sync_offsets_v1.json with quality metrics and reviewer sign-off; fused runs refuse events without an accepted offset.

title: Frame timestamps are frame_index / nominal FPS, not presentation timestamps
evidence: src/railway_detection/vision/video.py:37,96-108; cache train_events_event_010 camera_back last timestamp 23.83 s vs container duration 23.52 s
observed_fact: Several files have average frame rate different from nominal rate. One stream's last sampled timestamp exceeds its container duration by 0.31 s.
why_it_matters: Sub-second errors accumulate over a clip and bias latency metrics and A/V alignment.
recommended_correction: Record decoder presentation time per sampled frame alongside frame index; use it as the canonical timestamp.
closure_test_or_evidence: Per-stream check: last timestamp <= container duration; max |pts - idx/fps| reported in stream_status.

title: Audio evidence is stamped at window start and only the front camera's audio is used
observed_fact: A 1.0 s window is timestamped at its start, so a decision at time t can use sound up to 1 s in the future. Back-camera audio is extracted and never inferred.
why_it_matters: Non-causal evidence inflates any audio lead-time result; documentation describes front and back audio paths.
recommended_correction: Stamp audio evidence at window end; run audio inference per stream.
closure_test_or_evidence: Unit test: evidence timestamp equals window end; 54 audio outputs in the run.

title: Temporal confirmation can be satisfied by a single detection
observed_fact: Each fused frame includes every record in the preceding 0.25 s while frames are 0.2 s apart, so one vision record can appear in two consecutive fused frames and satisfy confirm_frames = 2.
why_it_matters: The claimed two-frame confirmation and its false-alarm suppression are not what runs.
recommended_correction: Consume each evidence record exactly once (window equals stride, half-open interval), or count confirmation on distinct source frame indices.
closure_test_or_evidence: Unit test: one isolated detection never produces WARNING with confirm_frames = 2.

title: Clearance logic does not implement positive rear confirmation
evidence: src/railway_detection/fusion/rules.py:48-49; src/railway_detection/fusion/decision_engine.py:210-258; active caches: 94 percent of detections are 'side', 1.2 percent 'rear'
observed_fact: 'side' belongs to both the approach and departure label sets. With continuous side detections the engine cycles TRAIN_PRESENT, CROSSING_OCCUPIED, TRAIN_DEPARTING, REAR_CONFIRMED and back, so whether the gate ever opens depends on where in that cycle the last detection falls. In REAR_CONFIRMED the 3 s dwell starts while a rear or side detection is still present.
why_it_matters: The stated invariant 'clearance requires positive rear confirmation and dwell' is false for the implemented system, and gate behaviour is partly arbitrary.
recommended_correction: Replace with the predeclared occupancy and clearance rule in EXPERIMENT_DESIGN_FINAL section 5; verify on synthetic traces only; freeze before formal replay.
closure_test_or_evidence: Table-driven tests for the clearance rule; property test that clearance never starts while any train-class evidence is present.

title: No liveness: closed states have no exit without a specific label sequence and the fault state is absorbing
observed_fact: WARNING always proceeds to closure even if evidence vanishes. TRAIN_PRESENT, CROSSING_OCCUPIED and TRAIN_DEPARTING wait indefinitely. FAULT_FAIL_SAFE never exits. The '15 healthy cycle recovery hysteresis' described in the corrective audit is not in the code.
why_it_matters: A system that stays closed achieves zero premature openings trivially. Safety results from this engine say nothing about a usable controller.
recommended_correction: Add bounded waits and an explicit recovery rule as specified in the design; report liveness as a first-class metric.
closure_test_or_evidence: Property test: from any state, with healthy sensors and no train evidence, the engine reaches IDLE within a stated bound.

title: Sensor health is not measured; unknown is treated as healthy
observed_fact: All evidence is ingested before replay, so each source's availability is its last record's flag until 2 s after its final timestamp. A frame that raises during inference is logged and dropped with no unavailable record. A missing video returns an empty list, the source is never registered, and the engine stays in IDLE with the gate open. The engine does not treat zero detections as a fault, which is correct.
why_it_matters: Of the eight cases the design must separate, only healthy-with-no-detections, single and dual dropout under explicit injection, and detection dropout behave as intended. Stale frames, decoder errors, inference errors and absent streams are invisible or fail open.
recommended_correction: Register expected sources from the run configuration; emit explicit unavailable records with a reason; compute health causally per tick from frame age.
closure_test_or_evidence: Eight-case table test (design section 6) passes against production classes.

title: Sources are classified by substring matching on their identifiers
observed_fact: A source is vision if its id contains 'camera', 'vision', 'front' or 'rear'. An audio source named audio_front would count as a camera. Camera 2 is matched on 'rear' while the files are named back.
why_it_matters: Works for the current ids camera_1, camera_2, audio_1; breaks silently on renaming.
recommended_correction: Carry modality and role as typed fields from source registration.
closure_test_or_evidence: Test with an audio source id containing 'front'.

title: The transition-legality table is not enforced by the decision engine
evidence: src/railway_detection/simulation/state_machine.py:31-96; no import outside tests and scripts/run_canonical_tests.py; tests/test_fault_injection_scenarios.py:44-117 defines its own copy
observed_fact: ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS and CrossingStateMachine are unused by MultimodalDecisionEngine. The scenario tests exercise a second, different copy defined inside the test file.
why_it_matters: The 'formal state machine with safety invariants' is documentation, not a runtime guard.
recommended_correction: Engine asserts every transition against one table in src; tests import that table.
closure_test_or_evidence: Illegal transition raises in a unit test; no duplicate table in tests.

title: Protocol and code disagree on whether audio may initiate a warning
observed_fact: Protocol section 12.1 and INV-2 give confirmed audio warning and closing authority. The engine's Rule 2 forbids any actuation from audio alone; audio can only postpone clearance.
why_it_matters: The hypothesised benefit of audio (earlier warning) cannot occur in the implemented system.
recommended_correction: Researcher decides; design document then fixes one rule for all conditions.
closure_test_or_evidence: Frozen configuration states the audio authority; a unit test asserts it.

title: The detector fires in all three no-train recordings and the existing output shows closure in every one
observed_fact: no_train event_001 back: 28 frames labelled front (confidence up to 0.69). event_002 front: 60 of 60 frames labelled side (up to 0.86). event_003: 13 frames. Whether a rail vehicle is visible in event_002 has not been checked by a human.
why_it_matters: Either a negative control is mislabelled or the detector has a high false-positive rate on road traffic. Both undermine any nuisance-closure claim.
recommended_correction: Researcher confirms each negative clip is train-free. Report closures as counts with exposure; consider collecting longer negative footage.
closure_test_or_evidence: Signed negative-control confirmation; nuisance table generated from the formal run.

title: Audio V3 inference does not apply the training normalisation
evidence: scripts/train_audio_model_v3_esc50.py:232-241,385-393 (saves norm_mean, norm_std); src/railway_detection/audio/model.py:156-157,184-186 (reads feature_mean, feature_std; defaults 0.0 and 1.0); src/railway_detection/experiments/layer_b_processor.py:104-107
observed_fact: The trainer stores normalisation under norm_mean and norm_std. The inference wrapper looks up feature_mean and feature_std, finds neither, and keeps mean 0 and std 1. The processor passes no statistics. Active caches contain 9 positive windows in 3 of 23 train events. Established from code on both sides; the checkpoint's keys were not read because no working torch install exists.
why_it_matters: Every Audio V3 output on the evaluation recordings was produced with inputs on the wrong scale. Statements about audio recall, false positives and modality contribution have no valid basis.
dependencies_affected_outputs: All audio outputs; B1, B2, B4-B7; IMA-38
recommended_correction: Read the keys the trainer writes; fail if a checkpoint lacks them; assert loaded mean, std and threshold in a test against the real checkpoint.
closure_test_or_evidence: Test loads the frozen checkpoint and asserts mean and std equal the stored values and threshold equals 0.37; constructor raises on a checkpoint without normalisation.

title: Three different audio thresholds are in effect
observed_fact: The checkpoint's stored threshold overrides the argument. The pipeline emits a detection only when the classifier label is train. The decision engine then applies its own default of 0.50, because the runner constructs it with no arguments. Stateless B2 uses any emitted detection.
why_it_matters: The stateful conditions run at 0.50 while the documented frozen value is 0.37, and conditions being compared use different thresholds.
recommended_correction: One frozen configuration object passed to every component; no numeric defaults for frozen parameters.
closure_test_or_evidence: Run manifest echoes the effective threshold of every component; a test fails if any differs.

title: Inference caches have no provenance and are reused by default
evidence: src/railway_detection/experiments/layer_b_processor.py:165-172,212-219,234-241,264-267; results/experiments/cache (60 files dated 2026-09-23 without cohort prefix, 81 dated 2026-10-13 08:45)
observed_fact: Cache keys contain cohort, event, stream and source id only. Model hash, threshold, sampling rate and media hash are absent. use_cache defaults to true. A stream interrupted by an exception is cached as if complete. Audio caches store only above-threshold detections, so per-window scores for negative windows are lost. Legacy and active files share one directory.
why_it_matters: A run can silently consume outputs from another model or configuration, and a truncated stream cannot be told from a complete one.
recommended_correction: Content-addressed run directories with a manifest, per-stream completion records and raw per-frame and per-window scores (design section 4).
closure_test_or_evidence: Changing any frozen parameter or checkpoint yields a different run id; a test shows no read path reaches results/experiments/cache.

title: The parameter-freeze and leakage checks cannot fail
evidence: scripts/run_real_world_experiments.py:67-70; src/railway_detection/experiments/leakage_guard.py:28-45,89-131; grep for TemporalEvidenceBuffer (used only in demo/video_demo.py)
observed_fact: The orchestrator passes FROZEN_PARAMETERS as the runtime parameters, so the comparison is a dictionary against itself, then prints that 16 parameters matched. Three 'frozen' temporal parameters (smoothing alpha, miss tolerance, evidence expiry) are not used anywhere in the experiment path. The leakage check token-matches one manifest and searches the image folder for .mov files. The Audio V2 hash is not blocked.
why_it_matters: The printed assurances are unconditional. Nothing prevents a wrong threshold or checkpoint.
recommended_correction: Verify values read back from the constructed components; block the prohibited hash; compare media hashes of evaluation files against training manifests.
closure_test_or_evidence: Negative tests: wrong threshold, V2 checkpoint, and an evaluation file listed in a training manifest each abort the run.

title: The result tree mixes outputs from different code versions
evidence: mtime: results/experiments/B*/summary.json 08:45; src decision_engine.py 09:31, failure_injector.py 09:29, metrics.py 09:37; results/experiments/corrected_run (B6b, B7b, B7f only, 09:32); results/experiments/B4/timelines (42 files 2026-09-23, 54 files 2026-10-13)
observed_fact: The 17 condition summaries were written before the decision engine, injector and metrics were edited. They still show missed_train false for all 27 events with a 0 to 12.5 percent interval. Only three conditions were re-run.
why_it_matters: No file under results/experiments is a valid result of the code now on disk.
recommended_correction: Treat results/experiments and results/archive as frozen legacy evidence; write all new outputs under results/runs/<run_id>.
closure_test_or_evidence: LEGACY manifest lists every file with hash; no new file is written under results/experiments.

title: No run registry for fusion experiments; the registry is polluted by test runs
evidence: results/experiment_registry.jsonl (139 rows: data validate 74, vision train 65; paths under pytest temp dirs); src/railway_detection/cli/main.py:209,380
observed_fact: The registry holds no record of any real-world experiment and contains rows written by unit tests.
why_it_matters: There is no machine-readable history of which run produced which output.
recommended_correction: Run manifest per run directory; tests write only to temporary paths.
closure_test_or_evidence: Registry diff is empty after running the test suite.

title: Premature opening is defined differently for baselines and for the proposed system
observed_fact: Stateless conditions are flagged premature whenever detection lapses after first detection, with no reference to ground truth. Audio-only is hardcoded false. The stateful conditions call the simulator without entry or clearance times, so their flag is always false and warning lead time is always none.
why_it_matters: The headline comparison (the state machine eliminates premature openings) is decided by the code path, not by behaviour.
recommended_correction: One evaluator applied to every condition's decision trace, taking ground truth as input (design section 8).
closure_test_or_evidence: The same trace submitted under two condition names yields identical metrics.

title: Ground truth is never linked and every event is scored as a train event
evidence: src/railway_detection/experiments/runner.py:88-95,110; src/railway_detection/data/layer_b.py:89; no labels/event_labels.json under data/raw/layer_b; no GroundTruthLoader in src
observed_fact: Labels are read from a file that exists for no event, under names (crossing_entry, tail_clearance) that match no T0-T4 key. has_train_ground_truth is hardcoded true, so the three negatives and the engine event enter train denominators and the false-alarm branch is unreachable.
why_it_matters: No metric that depends on labels has ever been computed, and cohort semantics are wrong.
recommended_correction: Event-type-aware loader for approved ground truth only; evaluator dispatches on event type.
closure_test_or_evidence: Loader and evaluator tests for train, no-train and engine events; negatives never appear in a train denominator.

title: Undefined metrics can still surface as numbers or disappear
observed_fact: wilson_score_interval returns (0, 0) for a zero denominator. statistics.py computes a missed-train interval from eligible_events with a default count of 0 and a default n of 21. A missing step near the entry time falls back to 'not missed' if the gate ever closed. Late warnings are clamped to a lead time of 0. Events whose gate never opens drop out of mean clearance latency. The orchestrator formats a None rate with a percent format.
why_it_matters: A missing label can still yield a zero-based interval; censored observations bias means; late warnings are hidden.
recommended_correction: Tri-state metric values with explicit status; no clamping; censored values reported as bounds; formatters refuse to print undefined values as numbers.
closure_test_or_evidence: Tests: zero denominator returns undefined and formatting it as a number raises; negative lead time preserved; never-opened event reported as right-censored.

title: The recordings are too short at both ends for the protocol's primary endpoints
evidence: src/railway_detection/experiments/leakage_guard.py:36-39 (2.0 s warning, 3.0 s closing, 3.0 s dwell, 3.0 s opening); src/railway_detection/simulation/gate_model.py:33-35; candidate T1 and T4 values; ffprobe durations
observed_fact: With detection at the first frame the barrier cannot be blocking before about 3.6 s nor fully closed before about 5.2 s. Candidate T1 is 3.2 s or less in 18 of the 22 events that have one, and T0 is 0.0 in 19 of those 22. Candidate T4 falls 1.0 to 2.7 s before the end of the back recording in 20 of 22 events, shorter than the 3.0 s clearance dwell. Depends on unapproved candidates; the arithmetic on code constants is exact.
why_it_matters: Missed-train rate as defined ('closed by T1') would be near 100 percent for any detector, and the proposed system could almost never reopen within a clip, so a premature-opening rate near zero and clearance latency are uninformative.
recommended_correction: Redefine primary endpoints around warning issued before entry and reopening during occupancy, with explicit censoring and a feasibility screen (design section 8).
closure_test_or_evidence: Per-event feasibility table published with the results; endpoints with fewer than a predeclared number of evaluable events reported as not estimable.

title: Safety-invariant verification is vacuous
observed_fact: The orchestrator loads per-event results and executes 'pass', then calls verify_safety_invariants('B4', []) with an empty list and prints PASSED for six invariants. Four of the six can never be set false by the function.
why_it_matters: Reported invariant passes carry no information.
recommended_correction: Trace-based invariant checks over stored decision logs, each with a deliberately violating fixture.
closure_test_or_evidence: Each invariant check fails on its violating fixture and reports the number of steps examined (must be greater than zero).

title: Statistical procedures differ from the protocol and ignore the design
observed_fact: The protocol names McNemar and Wilcoxon tests; the code uses a sign test and a bootstrap on total closed seconds across all 27 events, including negatives, and emits a 'statistically_significant' flag.
why_it_matters: Mixed cohorts and an undeclared test make the comparison uninterpretable.
recommended_correction: Implement the predeclared analysis in design section 9 only.
closure_test_or_evidence: Statistics module has one entry point whose inputs are per-event metric records filtered by eligibility.

title: Two fault modes do nothing, yet reports describe them as handled
observed_fact: STALE_TIMESTAMPS has an enum value and a schedule but no implementation, so B7e equals B4. The out-of-order swap is undone when the simulator sorts frames, so B7d equals B4 and Rule 8 is never reached in a run. Tables state 'Rejected by Rule 8' and 'Rejected by Tracker'.
why_it_matters: Robustness claims for timestamp disorder and staleness are unsupported.
recommended_correction: Implement staleness as delayed delivery; inject disorder at the delivery layer after ordering; assert the injection changed the input.
closure_test_or_evidence: Each fault condition's log shows a non-zero count of affected records and a decision trace that differs from the unperturbed run or an explicit 'no behavioural difference' record.

title: Frame-drop and other injections have imprecise semantics
observed_fact: The 100 percent drop defect is fixed. Remaining: drops remove whole fused instants rather than per-source frames; the generator is re-seeded with 42 for every event; only the first drop schedule's rate and seed are honoured; an absent drop_rate means drop everything; false detections are always attributed to camera_1; dropout windows are fractions of clip duration, unrelated to train position; injection statistics are not saved.
why_it_matters: '30 percent frame loss' is not 30 percent loss of camera frames, and results cannot be audited.
recommended_correction: Per-source, per-record injection with a seed derived from run id, event and source; required parameters; statistics persisted with the trace.
closure_test_or_evidence: Injection log per event; realised drop rate within a stated tolerance; reproducible given the run id.

title: Dual-blackout condition tests only entry into the fault state
observed_fact: With both cameras removed for the whole clip the engine closes after two ticks and stays closed.
why_it_matters: This verifies one transition. It is software verification, not evidence of safe behaviour under real sensor failure.
recommended_correction: Report as software verification; add a mid-event blackout with recovery to exercise the recovery rule.
closure_test_or_evidence: Fault-condition table labels each row as software verification.

title: The documented ablation matrix is not implemented and the implemented one is confounded
observed_fact: No E1-E7 condition exists in code. B0 to B4 changes camera count, confirmation, state machine and audio together; B3 to B4 adds audio and the state machine at once; B2 uses three-frame confirmation against two elsewhere. Stateless baselines reopen the instant detection lapses. The report's condition descriptions do not match the schedules actually run (for example B7a is labelled high false alarms but injects audio dropout).
why_it_matters: No subsystem contribution can be attributed from existing comparisons.
recommended_correction: Canonical factor-coded conditions with an explicit E and B mapping (design section 3); one condition table shared by runner and reports.
closure_test_or_evidence: Condition table is the only source of condition definitions; a test asserts adjacent ablations differ in exactly one factor.

title: The audio modality currently has almost no path to affect an outcome
evidence: src/railway_detection/fusion/decision_engine.py:176-181,244-249; active audio caches (9 positive windows, events 004, 017, 018)
observed_fact: In the stateful engine audio can only restart the clearance dwell while in REAR_CONFIRMED. Combined with IMA-22 and IMA-23 it almost never fires.
why_it_matters: A full-system versus no-audio contrast will be close to null for reasons unrelated to the value of audio.
recommended_correction: Fix IMA-22 and IMA-23, settle D5, then run the single-factor audio contrast and report whatever it shows.
closure_test_or_evidence: Audio contrast reported with the count of events in which audio changed any decision.

title: Report, table and figure generators contain hardcoded results and synthetic data
observed_fact: The report template writes fixed findings (100 percent event recall on 21 events, 76.4 and 91.8 percent continuity, 42.9 percent, p = 0.0039, 18 of 21, 0.20 s) regardless of data. Tables contain literal outcome cells. Figures plot a hardcoded list of 27 clearance latencies, fixed 100 percent detection bars, fixed fault latencies, and random normal samples when audio scores are absent.
why_it_matters: docs/REAL_WORLD_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md and the derived tables and figures are not evidence. Publishing them would be reporting fabricated values.
recommended_correction: Generators read only metric files from a run directory, carry the run id into every artifact, and contain no result literals.
closure_test_or_evidence: Static check: no numeric literal reaches a rendered cell or plotted series; regenerating from a second run changes the artifacts accordingly.

title: Earlier audits contain untraceable numbers and a fix that was not made
evidence: docs/FORENSIC_EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.md section 3 (lines 184-206); docs/CORRECTIVE_EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.md sections 6.3, 6.4, 10.2 and closing line; scratch/*.py (no metric recomputation code)
observed_fact: The forensic audit's recomputed per-condition table (for example B0 20 of 22 premature, B1 19 of 22 missed, B4 0 of 22) has no generating script or per-event file and relies on unapproved candidates. The corrective audit states a recovery hysteresis was added and cites test_idle_sustained_vision_loss_enters_fail_safe; neither exists. It closes with 'Certified ... under strict CENELEC/AREMA forensic audit guidelines'.
why_it_matters: These documents read as authoritative. Their cache-contamination and metric-default diagnoses are correct; their replacement numbers and certification language are not usable.
recommended_correction: Keep both files unchanged; the master audit's supersession table states which sections stand and which are withdrawn.
closure_test_or_evidence: Supersession table present; no new document cites the withdrawn sections.

title: Active protocol documents describe components that do not exist
observed_fact: GroundTruthLoader, tests/test_safety_invariants.py, configs/frozen_parameters_v3.json and run_final_real_world_evaluation.py are absent. The protocol describes a four-state machine with EMA smoothing; the code has eleven states and no smoothing.
why_it_matters: A reader would assume the documented safeguards are in force.
recommended_correction: EXPERIMENT_DESIGN_FINAL.md becomes the governing specification; protocol v9 is retained as history.
closure_test_or_evidence: Each requirement in the design document maps to a file and a test in the implementation plan.

title: Sixteen 'safety' tests import no production code
observed_fact: The twelve scenario tests and four forensic regression tests define their own classes and helper functions and assert on those. They account for 16 of the '36 passed' and part of the '49 passed' totals. tests/unit/test_experiment_runner_v2.py asserts a premature-opening rate of 0.0 that is true by construction and, for B6b, only that one event was processed.
why_it_matters: These tests cannot fail when the system is wrong. Pass counts built on them overstate verification.
recommended_correction: Keep the files as history but exclude them from the gate; write tests against production classes for each scenario.
closure_test_or_evidence: Mutation check: reverting each fix in the plan makes at least one gated test fail.

title: The canonical test totals cannot be reproduced from the current tree
observed_fact: Twelve tracked test modules are missing from disk and no environment can run the suite. No test was executed during this audit.
why_it_matters: Reported totals are historical statements only.
recommended_correction: Re-establish the suite in Phase 1 and record collected, passed, failed and skipped counts with the commit hash.
closure_test_or_evidence: Test report generated by CI-style command stored with the commit hash.

title: Negative controls and seven other events come from one short evening session; total negative exposure is about one minute per camera
evidence: ffprobe creationdate and device tags; durations: no-train front 60.3 s, back 60.5 s; train cohort front 1,252 s, back 1,224 s
observed_fact: Train events 001-020 were recorded on 2026-09-14 between 14:13 and 17:26 local with two handheld phones. Events 021-023, all three negatives and the engine event were recorded on 2026-10-04 between 19:22 and 19:59 local, the back view on an iPad. Candidate metadata names a single crossing.
why_it_matters: Negatives are confounded with lighting, session and device. One minute of exposure cannot bound a false-alarm rate (zero episodes would still allow roughly 180 per hour at 95 percent).
recommended_correction: Report counts with exposure and no hourly rate; stratify by session; disclose single site. Longer negative footage is the highest-value new data.
closure_test_or_evidence: Limitations section and cohort table state sessions, devices, lighting and exposure.

title: Vision test-set performance does not describe field behaviour
observed_fact: The detector's reported 99.46 percent mAP and 100 percent rear recall come from an export whose splits were grouped by inferred source names. In the field outputs rear is 1.2 percent of detections and several events contain none.
why_it_matters: In-domain image metrics cannot be cited as evidence of crossing-level reliability.
recommended_correction: Cite image metrics as development-set results only; report per-class field statistics from the formal run.
closure_test_or_evidence: Paper text separates development metrics from field results.

title: The audio model is trained on a different acoustic domain
observed_fact: Positive examples are short horn clips from online sources; evaluation audio is handheld phone audio at a roadside.
why_it_matters: Even after IMA-22 is fixed, transfer is unknown and may be poor. That is a result to report, not to tune away.
recommended_correction: No retraining or threshold change on evaluation data. Report field behaviour at the frozen threshold.
closure_test_or_evidence: Audio field table produced at threshold 0.37 only.

title: The decision policy will be revised after its outputs on the evaluation recordings have been seen
evidence: results/experiments (pilot outputs of 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-13); IMA-15, IMA-16
observed_fact: Fixing the clearance and liveness defects changes the evaluated system after pilot runs on the same 27 events.
why_it_matters: Results on these recordings are no longer a clean held-out test of the final policy.
recommended_correction: Specify the revised policy a priori, verify it on synthetic traces only, freeze it by commit and configuration hash before the formal replay, and disclose the pilot. A small confirmatory recording set would restore a held-out test.
closure_test_or_evidence: Freeze record (commit, configuration hash, date) predates the formal run; disclosure present in the paper.
